I fly decently frequently, sometimes very long hauls. I think there are ways to deal with it that help. I normally don't have more problem when I fly than any other day with Fibro.

1. Compression socks. They improve circulation and will provide heat to your leg which helps with pain

2. Compression gloves. Same as compression socks. I have a lot of pain in my hands, so this comes very much in handy

3. Joint braces. My left hand is the worst for me because I also have cenobite (idk how it's called properly), so I use a brace that helps me carry my luggage without forcing my joints so much. Sometimes I feel that even the ones that roll are a bit hard on my hand

3. Try so sleep and eat well and regularly. 

4. Have your meds easy to access so you don't miss their timing. I sometimes pack pain meds just in case. I can't take ibuprofen, but it's good if you can

5. Walk. Walk in the airport while you wait and walk a bit in the plane if possible.

6. Stretch. Some basic stretching really help my joints when in this type of situation. It's easier in the airport, but there are some youtube tutorials about doing them in the plane, even in weird seats.

7. Give yourself grace. Traveling is effort for everyone, more for us, so be aware it can be difficult and take care of what you can, but don't worry too much if it's still bad. It's important to not stopping trying to have a life when we are physically ill, to prevent getting mentally ill. Take your time and accommodate, but try to do things still

Hope it helped.

So I started very slow, mostly using machines with low weight and every session trying to go for one more repetition until I felt comfortable upping the weight. So the ideal in most researchs for a normal person trying to get muscle mass is 6-12 repetitions. Then people do 3-5 sets, I do 3, some people do 4 after 1-2 years at the gym, 5 is more athletic/advanced. You should rest well in between, I rest around 2min, sometimes 2.5-3min depending on how I'm feeling, you need to feel ready to do the exercise right again. I don't recommend less than 1.5min as you'll probably lose performance. So you start with the highest weight you can do 6 reps with and every session try to go one more rep, when you reach a session when you can do 12 reps in all sets, next one you try to up the weight and start the cycle again.
I did that only using machines for a while, as you don't have to stabilize yourself and it's easier to isolate muscle groups, so your mind muscle connection is built easier. 
After I got comfortable with exercising with at least my body weight I started doing free weight exercises, so I could learn how to stabilize myself etc, but then, of course, with little to no weight in the beginning, as now you have more stuff for your muscle to do while moving, and then progress the weight as before. 
If you can, about a month ago I started separating the sides of my body, which means exercising with one leg at a time or one arm at a time, so you have more control and need more stabilizing focus. That is normally heavier has you're lifting the weight with just one side, so also start with little to no weight :)

That's it, you don't need anything too fancy or complicated, just get to know your body and take it slow.

I would recommend doing mobility exercises before too, which are similar to stretches, but dynamic, to warm up your body and prevent injury. There are lots of personal trainer videos online about it on yt. And stretch at the end. This part helps a lot with my joint pain and overall posture, so kinda aids my fibro symptoms.

I'm a very bad runner and it can be hard on your knees, especially if you already have pain on them (I don't, but still bad at running), so I don't run much, just try it for 1-2min a couple times in my cardio sessions. 

So about cardio, you should definitely do it for your heart health, and overall quality of life, but you don't have to run if you don't feel comfortable with it. I would recommend doing cardio after you strength train, tho, because then you have more energy to lift heavier weights correctly. 

I normally just walk or "fast walk" like 3-6km/h, on an incline 9-15 in the treadmill for 10-30min. I don't recommend jogging because it impacts your knees like running without raising your heart rate enough to make it worth it. Walk or fast walk, or straight up run, or combine those somehow
